discussion:
**Issued Mon Nov 2, 2026.** A Pacific cold front crossed the Southwest Sunday with widespread showers and thunderstorms, flood watches over much of western New Mexico and central Arizona, and heavy rain over the Gila. Following repeated wetting rain in late October, fuels across the GACC are moist and ERCs are assumed well below the 60th percentile.

**Today:** Strong west winds behind the front. A High Wind Warning covers the South Central Mountains until 6 pm with gusts to 60 mph, and gusts of 40-65 mph reach the southeast plains and Guadalupe Mountains. Wind speeds meet the W trigger, but saturated fuels and post-frontal air keep this from being a High Risk day.

**Tue-Thu:** Dry and quiet. Light winds, seasonable to slightly below-normal temperatures. Fine fuels dry out but ERCs stay low.

**Fri-Sun:** A weak disturbance brings a chance of showers to central Arizona Friday. Confidence drops after Thursday, but no critical wind/low RH pattern appears.
